proposed_widenings.name: AnchoredSignal.transport
proposed_widenings.justification: The portal transports any creature that enters it to the destination permanent teleportation circle. AnchoredSignal in types.ts only has audible | mental variants. The v4 atom transport_exile already exists in the taxonomy — this is a surface gap, not an atom gap. A transport variant is needed to represent portal passage to a named permanent circle chosen at cast time.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Any creature that enters the portal instantly appears within 5 feet of the destination circle or in the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied.

proposed_widenings.name: AnchorTarget.area.shape.circle
proposed_widenings.justification: The portal anchor is a 5-foot-radius circle drawn on the ground. AnchorTarget.area currently only supports a cube shape (used by Alarm). A circle (radius) shape is needed. Note: Attachment.area already supports sphere/radius — the gap is specific to AnchorTarget.
proposed_widenings.evidence: you draw a 5-foot-radius circle on the ground inscribed with sigils

proposed_widenings.name: AnchoredSignal.transport.destination
proposed_widenings.justification: The transport destination must be a known permanent teleportation circle identified by sigil sequence, on the same plane of existence. This is a cast-time choice from a player-known registry. No existing surface type can represent a named-permanent-circle destination reference. A destination sub-shape with kind: 'permanent_teleportation_circle' and a chosenAtCast marker is needed.
proposed_widenings.evidence: a permanent teleportation circle of your choice whose sigil sequence you know and that is on the same plane of existence as you

notes: The anchored_trigger family is structurally the closest honest fit: cast draws a portal circle (anchor), creature enters (enters_area event), transport fires (release). Both blocking gaps are surface-level: AnchoredSignal needs a transport variant, and AnchorTarget.area needs a circle shape. The v4 transport_exile atom exists so no atom widening is required. One semantic caveat: Alarm is modeled as a one-shot trigger (fires once), but Teleportation Circle is a continuous portal that transports every creature that enters during its 1-round duration. A multi_fire / continuous flag on AnchoredTriggerMechanics may be needed to distinguish these, but this is a secondary concern relative to the two blocking surface gaps.
